parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: A proton in a nucleus decays to form a neutron and a $\beta^+$ particle.
parts.text: State the name of another lepton that is produced in the decay.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the interaction (force) that gives rise to this decay.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State which of the three particles (proton, neutron or $\beta^+$ particle) has the largest ratio of charge to mass.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text: Use the quark model to show that the charge on the proton is $+e$, where $e$ is the elementary charge.

parts.label: (a)(v)
parts.text:
The quark composition of the proton is changed during the decay.

Describe the change to the quark composition.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem: A nucleus X ($^{12}_{6}\text{X}$) and a nucleus Y ($^{16}_{8}\text{Y}$) are accelerated by the same uniform electric field.
parts.text:
Determine the ratio

$$\frac{\text{electric force acting on nucleus X}}{\text{electric force acting on nucleus Y}}.$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Determine the ratio

$$\frac{\text{acceleration of nucleus X due to the field}}{\text{acceleration of nucleus Y due to the field}}.$$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Nucleus X is at rest in the uniform electric field at time $t = 0$.

The field causes nucleus X to accelerate so that it moves through the field.

On Fig. 6.1, sketch the variation with time $t$ of the acceleration $a$ of nucleus X due to the field.
